![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14222139/assets/5d154a914d58f5b695adec9dd873ac067ba8280a4fefffd4f2f5559ff5ee04da.png)

The region enclosed by the curve $y=\frac{1}{1-x},$ the vertical line $x=2,$ and the horizontal line $y=-2$ is rotated $2\pi $ radians about the line $x=2,$ as shown in the picture. Which of the following integrals gives the volume of the resulting solid?
question.worked_solution:
Since our region rotates about a vertical line, we need to write the equation of the given curve in terms of $y:$ 

$$
y=\frac{1}{1-x}\,⟹\,x=1-\frac{1}{y}
$$

 

Also, notice that the limits of integration are from $y=-2$ to $y=-1$ along the $y$-axis.

To determine which is the left and which is the right function, let's draw our horizontal arrow.  

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14222139/assets/239113c4d2bbca26c694796f6f17bd26bebf47697dad53f7af832088213fd4c9.png)

The horizontal arrow 

- *enters* the region through the left function $x=1-\frac{1}{y},$ and

- *leaves* through the right function $x=2.$

Therefore, the integral that gives our volume is

$$
\begin{aligned}V & =\pi {\int }_{-2}^{-1}[\,(\text{right function})-(\text{left function})\,]^{2}\,\text{d}y \\  & =\pi {\int }_{-2}^{-1}{[\,(2)-(1-\frac{1}{y})\,]}^{2}\,\text{d}y \\  & =\pi {\int }_{-2}^{-1}{(1+\frac{1}{y})}^{2}\,\,\text{d}y \\  & =\pi {\int }_{-2}^{-1}(1+\frac{2}{y}+\frac{1}{{y}^{2}})\,\,\text{d}y.\end{aligned}
$$
